sender.ms: SMS yang mengaku daripada Maybank, CIMB atau bank lain, kadangkala dalam bebenang yang sama dengan SMS bank sebenar
sender.en: A text claiming to be from Maybank, CIMB or another bank, sometimes in the same thread as the bank's real texts

name.ms: SMS bank palsu: “tukar kata laluan di pautan ini” atau “transaksi mencurigakan, hubungi nombor ini”
name.en: Fake bank text: “change your password at this link” or “suspicious transaction, call this number”

how.ms: Anda menerima SMS yang kelihatan seperti daripada bank anda. Satu jenis mengatakan ada beberapa cubaan log masuk dan meminta anda menukar nama pengguna dan kata laluan segera di pautan, yang membawa ke laman bank palsu. Satu lagi memberi amaran tentang pengeluaran wang yang anda tidak buat dan meminta anda menelefon nombor dalam SMS; “pegawai bank” yang menjawab kemudian memperdaya anda. Penipu boleh memalsukan kod penghantar rasmi bank, jadi mesej itu boleh muncul bersama SMS sebenar. Bank di Malaysia tidak lagi menghantar pautan melalui SMS.
how.en: You get a text that looks like it is from your bank. One kind says there have been several login attempts and asks you to change your username and password at once through a link, which opens a fake bank site. Another warns of a withdrawal you did not make and asks you to call a number in the text; the “bank officer” who answers then deceives you. Scammers can spoof a bank's official sender codes, so the message can appear alongside real texts. Banks in Malaysia no longer send links by text message.

text.ms: SMS daripada “bank” tentang cubaan log masuk atau transaksi yang anda tidak buat.
text.en: A text from the “bank” about login attempts or a transaction you didn't make.
You are told to act immediately.

text.ms: Mesej itu mengandungi pautan untuk “tukar kata laluan” atau nombor untuk ditelefon.
text.en: It contains a link to “change your password” or a number to call.

text.ms: Laman palsu atau “pegawai bank” meminta kata laluan, TAC atau persetujuan transaksi.
text.en: The fake site or “bank officer” asks for your password, TAC or to approve a transaction.

text.ms: BANK: Terdapat 3 cubaan log masuk yang gagal ke akaun perbankan internet anda. Sila tukar kata laluan dan nama pengguna anda dengan segera di [pautan] untuk mengelakkan akaun disekat.
text.en: BANK: There were 3 failed login attempts on your internet banking account. Please change your password and username immediately at [pautan] to avoid your account being blocked.

text.ms: Pengeluaran tunai RM4,850.00 dari akaun anda sedang diproses. Jika anda tidak membuat transaksi ini, hubungi Pusat Khidmat Pelanggan di [number] segera.
text.en: A cash withdrawal of RM4,850.00 from your account is being processed. If you did not make this transaction, call Customer Service at [number] immediately.

ms: sms bank suruh tukar kata laluan di pautan
sms kata ada cubaan log masuk ke akaun bank
sms transaksi pengeluaran yang saya tak buat suruh telefon nombor
telefon nombor dalam sms bank rupanya penipu
sms palsu masuk dalam thread sms bank sebenar
en: bank text told me to change my password through a link
text says there were login attempts on my bank account
text about a withdrawal i did not make told me to call a number
called the number in the bank text and it was a scammer
fake text appeared in the same thread as my real bank texts

ms: SMS bank yang mengandungi pautan: bank di Malaysia tidak lagi menghantar pautan melalui SMS.
SMS yang meminta anda menelefon nombor di dalamnya untuk membatalkan transaksi.
Nama laman yang dieja salah atau bukan laman rasmi bank.
en: A bank text with a link: banks in Malaysia no longer send links by text.
A text asking you to call a number in it to cancel a transaction.
A misspelled site name or one that is not the bank's official site.

ms: Jangan tekan pautan, jangan telefon nombor dalam SMS, dan jangan balas.
Semak akaun dalam aplikasi rasmi bank, atau hubungi nombor di belakang kad anda.
Jika sudah memberikan kata laluan atau TAC, hubungi bank anda dan 997 segera.
en: Don't tap the link, don't call the number in the text, and don't reply.
Check your account in the bank's official app, or call the number on the back of your card.
If you already gave your password or TAC, call your bank and 997 straight away.
